title: Rav Gaza
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yevamot 45b: “Ravina said: Rav Gasa told me: Rabbi Yose bar Avin came to our place, and there was a case of an unmarried woman, and he declared [the child] fit,” etc. “Rav Sheshet said (in Hyman’s judgment undoubtedly Rav Sheshet of Katarzya, who lived in Rav Ashi’s time; or he proposes Rav Ashi): Rav Gaza told me: It was not Rabbi Yose bar Avin but Rabbi Yose bar Zevida.” In Shabbat 145b: “Rav Yosef said — and Rav Gaza also said: Once I came there (to the Land of Israel) and made Babylonian kutach,” etc. Hyman strongly prefers Dikdukei Soferim’s Rav Gada reading; he was Rav Sheshet’s attendant.

notes.text: Hyman’s undoubtedly/Katarzya identification, alternative Rav Ashi and preference for Gada retain their force and attribution. The actual Gasa/Gaza/Gada forms remain distinct.

The consulted Shabbat 145b directly names Rav Gaza in the Babylonian-kutach episode. Gasa, Gaza and the proposed Gada remain distinct forms. Hyman’s “undoubtedly” Katarzya identification, alternative Rav Ashi and strong preference for the Dikdukei Soferim reading are retained as his judgments.
